text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: perf-p95 latency spike on inference-pool-7 (>5s) across multiple zones. alert_id=ALRT-4821. paging on-call.
Sam: I'm on it. pulling logs + tracing. which services are impacted?
Sam: quick check shows KV miss rate jumped to 98% and backend request latencies up. suspect kv prewarm/eviction regression.
Sam: running: `kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide` to check pod restarts
Sam: also hitting the model-serving pools, redis connections look fine but misses are high.
IncidentBot: Noted. CPU low on kv nodes, memory churn high.
Maria: FYI I saw a config push ~20m ago that changed `kv.cache.prefill=false` in infra-config. tagging @Jen who did the rollout.
Jen: that was my change, I rolled a small optimization to skip prefill for cold starts. didn't expect the miss storm. rolling back now.
Jen: `kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/kv-cache KV_PREFILL=true && kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/kv-cache`
DeployBot: Deploy started by Jen (deploy/infra-config) at 09:24 UTC. rollout id=dep-8921.
Sam: reverting traffic for affected customers to dedicated pool to reduce error surface. updating routing rule: `redwood route set -s inference-pool-7 -t inference-dedicated-2 --weight 0.2`
Lee: grabbing runbook: `kv-eviction-response.md` Step 2 references prefill toggle but the command snippet is outdated.
Sam: confirmed. Runbook didn't mention fallback routing. we should add that.
Maria: mitigation timeline: 09:24 alert, 09:26 rollback started, 09:29 prefill restored, 09:33 miss rate dropped to 12%, p95 back under 300ms by 09:36.
Sam: customer impact: ProductOps reported increased latency for 3 customers on Hosted API (IDs: C-441, C-502, C-719). no API errors surfaced, just long tail latency and timeouts for some client SDKs.
ProductOps: those customers were notified at 09:40 with a heads-up. no escalations yet.
Jen: posted PR to revert the change and add tests: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-1289
Maria: good. opening postmortem and scheduling a follow-up. proposed time: Friday 10:00am PT.
Sam: assigning immediate action items: 1) Update kv runbook steps + add routing fallback (owner: Maria, jira RED-1201) 2) Add alert for sudden KV miss-rate delta (>20% relative) (owner: Sam, jira RED-1202) 3) Auto-prewarm job for new pods (owner: Jen, jira RED-1203) 4) Customer comms template for latency incidents (owner: ProductOps, jira RED-1204)
Lee: will pick up on-call notes for handoff. leaving a checklist for next shift: current state = stabilized, rollback in prod, PR merged to revert change pending CI, monitor for 2h.
Sam: handoff summary for next on-call (Lee):
- cause: unintended side-effect of disabling KV prefill in infra-config rollout
- mitigation: rollback env var + restart daemonset, traffic reroute to dedicated pool, resumed normal p95
- customer impact: latency spike, 3 customers affected, notified
- open action items: RED-1201, RED-1202, RED-1203, RED-1204
Lee: thanks. I'll watch for regressions and start the runbook update doc in a branch.
Maria: scheduling postmortem: `postmortem create --incident ALRT-4821 --time "2026-03-20T17:00:00Z" --owner Maria`
ProductOps: will prepare the customer follow-up draft for review before postmortem.
Jen: I'll add the prewarm integration test and a canary to infra-config changes.
Sam: quick note — runbook needs a code snippet update. current snippet uses `kubectl set env daemonset/kv-cache KV_PREFILL=false` but we should prefer a patch apply because of rollout behavior. will add exact commands to the PR.
Maria: tagging SRE lead to review runbook PRs and the incident timeline. thanks everyone for the quick response. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident ALRT-4821 set to status: RESOLVED (stabilized). bridging to postmortem thread.
Lee: handing off to next oncall at 10:10 — monitoring for 2h.
Sam: closing the on-call thread, following up in the postmortem doc with logs and traces attached.
